precepts.text: Whoso feareth the Lord shall direct his friendship aright: for as he is, so shall his neighbour be also. My son, gather instruction from thy youth up: so shalt thou find wisdom till thine old age. If you fear the Lord you are going to direct your friendships aright, because as you are, so shall your neighbour be also. But if you are constantly having issues, constantly having problems, who is the issue? Who is causing these troubles? Because with the laws of God you should be able to direct your friendship aright. So why is your name always in something? And gather instruction from thy youth up: we did not have that opportunity. But we have to be born again coming into this truth and begin to do so. You cannot drag in all the ways your grandmother and your auntie used to deal with each other. It is a new day.
precepts.point: I used to be a murderer. The law said thou shalt not murder. I used to be a thief. The law said thou shalt not steal. I used to be an abuser. Once I know the Lord, now I repent. Guess what, brother? Same thing. Guess what, sister? Same thing with your trauma. Stop using your trauma as a crutch. That happened when you were 14, 15, 16. You are still using that. Now you are 46, you are 50, and you are still using that. Some of you are in your third marriage and you still cannot keep a man, you cannot keep a woman, because of your trauma. You cannot cope.

note.label: Destructive Behaviors Among Our People

precepts.why:
“The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul.” The law of God is perfect, it is pure, there is nothing wrong with it, and converting means to change. Only the law can change you. I used to be a murderer; the law said thou shalt not murder. I used to be a thief; the law said thou shalt not steal. I used to be an abuser. Once I know the Lord, I repent. Same thing, brother. Same thing, sister, with your trauma. Stop using your trauma as a crutch. It happened when you were 14, 15, 16, and now you're 46, 50, in your third marriage, still using it, and you can't keep a man or a woman because you cannot cope.

We never grew up around order, structure and unity. So when we come around it now, we begin to feel uncomfortable, because we realize we are the problem: the reason environments become toxic, the reason people bicker and fight, the instigating spirit we grew up seeing. Now, in a body and a truth where the light shines on that, you are forced to change, and brothers and sisters do not want to.

“Whoso feareth the Lord shall direct his friendship aright: for as he is, so shall his neighbour be also.” If you fear the Lord, you are going to direct your friendships aright, because as you are, so shall your neighbour be. But if you are constantly having issues, constantly having problems, who is the issue? Who is causing these troubles? With the laws of God and all the examples in the scriptures, you should be able to direct your friendship aright. So why is your name always in something?

“My son, gather instruction from thy youth up: so shalt thou find wisdom till thine old age.” We didn't have the opportunity to gather instruction from our youth up. But coming into this truth we have to be born again and begin to do so. You can't drag in all the ways your grandmama and your auntie and them used to deal with each other. It's a new day.

precepts.text: She is very unpleasant to the unlearned: he that is without understanding will not remain with her. Wisdom is very unpleasant to the unlearned. You did not learn about yourself. All you ever did was point out other people's problems. You never examined yourself. You never looked in the mirror. So now that wisdom finally reveals who you are, it is very unpleasant. And he that is without understanding will not remain with her: that is why people have to find a reason to leave. They get offended, they find a reason to be mad, and then they go. What is the root cause? Because they do not want to change once that wisdom is revealed.

“he that is without understanding will not remain with her.” That's why people have to find a reason to leave. They get offended, they find a reason to be mad, and then they go. What is the root cause? They don't want to change once that wisdom is revealed. And the law, which is perfect, converts only the soul that will be changed.

Destructive attitudes begin internally before they become visible externally. A person may still attend services, teach, lead, pray or serve while harboring the wrong spirit, an evil spirit. You look at the fringes and think, he's good, she's good; you would be surprised how many have an evil spirit in the midst of us. Some come here to destroy the unity of the brotherhood, because in the world it's always chaos: you never see a room full of black people with no fight, no argument, breaking bread together. Whatever you were going through in the world, you had better get over it, and quick, because that thing will destroy you. Those who carry that spirit will find themselves outside these doors.

precepts.text: Let reason go before every enterprise and counsel before every action: get counsel before you seal the deal, and save yourself a whole lot of heartache.
precepts.point: Extol not thyself in the counsel of thine own heart, lest thy soul be torn in pieces as a bull straying alone and thou be left as a dry tree: so many have fallen victim to their own counsel, driving the wrong way up the highway while the officer says turn around.

note.label: Why Do Fools Fall In Love

precepts.why:
Sirach warns, “Extol not thyself in the counsel of thine own heart; that thy soul be not torn in pieces as a bull straying alone.” That forward thinking, not looking for counsel, not trying to seek or find out, has destroyed so many people. So many have fallen victim to their own counsel and their own mind, thinking they have it figured out. You don’t got the answers, sway. The direction you are heading is the wrong way. Imagine driving on the wrong side of the highway with the officer telling you, turn around, and you say he doesn’t know what he’s talking about. Boom, you dead.

The remedy is Sirach 37: “Let reason go before every enterprize, and counsel before every action.” Before every enterprise, make sure it is sound, that it makes sense, that thought has been put into it. Never do anything on a whim, piecing things together with half-assed research.

“And counsel before every action.” Before you make a move, before you seal the deal, get counsel and find out if this is what you should do, and you will save yourself a whole lot of heartache.

Nobody in this camp has an excuse to say there is no one to talk to. There are men here who have gone through it and senior sisters who have dealt with it, who can help you make the right decision in a proving if you are honest and open about what you are experiencing. They can help you see the red flags, and also the things in yourself you may not see, so you can conquer them and continue the proving process instead of being left “as a dry tree.”

precepts.text: Wisdom lifteth up the head of him that is of low degree, and maketh him to sit among great men; a brother starting from the bottom at a job does not matter. Commend not a man for his beauty, neither abhor a man for his outward appearance. How many sisters were deceived by a good-looking man before the truth? Every woman wants a man, and a woman who says she does not need one goes against nature: her hormones release when she is under her husband, which is why she falls asleep ten minutes into the movie she asked to watch. She is bone of his bone, made in his image, which is why little girls look like their daddy; the body is the portal but the seed comes from the man. Sisters, release the feminism.
precepts.point: There is a friend who being turned to enmity and strife will discover thy reproach, and some friend is a companion at the table and will not continue in the day of thy affliction. Sirach 11:29, bring not every man into thine house, for the deceitful man hath many trains, sits with these; Sirach 6 through 15 connect, from proving a friend to not letting just anyone stroll into your house, with chapter 12 adding trust not thine enemy, for as iron rusteth so is his wickedness. You cannot know someone in three months or even a year: a person of twenty-seven has twenty-six years you know nothing of, family history, mental illness, diabetes, disease.

note.label: Our Forefathers Built This; We as Sons Must Preserve This!

precepts.why:
“If thou wouldest get a friend, prove him first and be not hasty to credit him.” In the forties they understood it takes time to know someone’s true intentions: you could court her, but on the front porch in front of everybody, no dates, no secret meetings. “For some man is a friend for his own occasion”: some just want sex, men and women, and we have them among us. When you look across the room, you are not wondering if she can help with your resume. You are thinking about the curves, the lips, the perfume. When you learn the truth and the fear of the Lord, you realize it is more than how she looks, and the same for the sisters.

Sirach says: “Wisdom lifteth up the head of him that is of low degree, and maketh him to sit among great men.” Whatever the brother’s finances, even if he is just starting at the bottom of a job, none of that matters. Wisdom lifts up his head and sets him among great men.

“Commend not a man for his beauty; neither abhor a man for his outward appearance.” Sisters, how many of you were deceived by a good-looking man before you came into this truth? Don’t raise your hand. And don’t let social media fool you: every woman wants a man. A woman who says she doesn’t need one is going against nature. Her body releases hormones when she is under her husband; that is why she falls asleep ten minutes into the movie she asked you to watch. All her fear goes out the window, because she is safe.

She is bone of his bone, flesh of his flesh, made in the man’s image, and she is his glory. That is why little girls look like their daddy: her body is the portal that brings us into this life, but the seed comes from the man. Sisters in the truth who walk around like they don’t need their husband, release the feminism.

So don’t pass over a good brother because of his outward appearance. A sister told a captain she couldn’t see herself with a good brother; did you see yourself forty-something and not married? Prove a man by his wisdom and intentions, not his looks.

precepts.text: Meditate continually in his commandments, and he shall establish thine heart and give thee wisdom.
precepts.point: Stay humble with it: Lord, my heart is not haughty, nor mine eyes lofty; neither do I exercise myself in great matters, or in things too high for me; David behaved and quieted himself as a child that is weaned of his mother. Except ye be converted and become as little children, ye shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven; so behave yourselves humbly, and the Most High will establish thine heart and increase thy wisdom.

note.label: Leviticus 5: The Trespass Offering and the Duty of the Witness

precepts.why:
Though he wist it not, yet is he guilty: saying I did not know does not remove sin. The remedy is to know the law. “Let thy mind be upon the ordinances of the Lord and meditate continually in his commandments: he shall establish thine heart, and give thee wisdom at thine owns desire.”

The ordinances are found in the first five books. As these four chapters a day are conducted, meditate and study them continually, and He will establish thine heart and give thee wisdom.

precepts.text: Do not spend your hours joking with your peers; cleave unto the wise men that sit over you, as Joshua did with Moses.
precepts.point: That is the spirit the young men coming up in this truth should aspire to: cleave to your leadership. It is not being around the longest that qualifies a man to rise up in another's stead; it is being the diligent servant who learned the ins and outs of how his leader was successful, and even observed his leader's mistakes so he knows what not to do in that position.

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

precepts.why:
“Stand in the multitude of the elders; and cleave unto him that is wise.” That is what Joshua did with Moses, and it is what the young men in this truth should do. Do not spend your hours joking with your peers; cleave unto the wise men that sit over you.

The diligent servant who cleaves to the wise learns how his leader was successful, and even observes his leader's mistakes so he knows what not to do in that position. That is how Moses' minister became the man to rise up in his stead.

precepts.text: Get to him early, because you never know how long that brother will be around; wherever he is, be there to receive whatever knowledge he has to offer.
precepts.point: That is the spirit the young men coming up in this truth should aspire to: cleave to your leadership. It is not being around the longest that qualifies a man to rise up in another's stead; it is being the diligent servant who learned the ins and outs of how his leader was successful, and even observed his leader's mistakes so he knows what not to do in that position.

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

precepts.why:
“And if thou seest a man of understanding, get thee betimes unto him, and let thy foot wear the steps of his door.” Get to him early, because you never know how long that brother will be around. Wherever he is, be there to receive whatever knowledge he has to offer.

Joshua's foot wore the steps of Moses' door: he departed not out of the tabernacle. Let thy foot wear the steps of his door, as Joshua did, and you learn what it takes to rise up in a leader's stead.

precepts.text: Meditate continually, as a habit, and he shall establish thine heart and give thee wisdom at thine own desire.
precepts.point: Make meditation a daily custom, a holy habit, as our forefathers did: somewhere alone and peaceful where the mind can be clear, because you cannot meditate in the middle of activity and noise. When you meditate continually on the commandments, the Lord establishes your heart, and the evil thoughts you battle begin to flush out of your mind.

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

precepts.why:
“Let thy mind be upon the ordinances of the Lord and meditate continually in his commandments: he shall establish thine heart, and give thee wisdom at thine owns desire.” Meditate continually, as a habit, a holy habit, the way Joshua was told to meditate day and night.

And there is the promise with it: he shall establish thine heart, and give thee wisdom at thine own desire. When you meditate continually on the commandments, the Lord establishes your heart, and the evil thoughts you battle begin to flush out of your mind.

precepts.text: A faithful friend is a strong defence, and he that hath found such an one hath found a treasure; that is what Jonathan was to David.
precepts.point: Jonathan would have been next in line for the throne; you would think his loyalty lay with his daddy, but he saw the spirit was not on his father, it was on his brother David. His loyalty exceeded his own desires. That is the kind of friend to look for, and the lesson to learn from Jonathan.

note.label: 1 Samuel 19: A Faithful Friend Is a Strong Defence

precepts.why:
“A faithfull friend is a strong defence: and he that hath found such an one hath found a treasure.” That is what Jonathan was to David.

“Saul spake to Jonathan his son, and to all his servants, that they should kill David.” The Philistines could not get him, so now he wants Israelites to kill an Israelite; that is how far down the slope this man has gone. “But Jonathan Saul’s son delighted much in David”, and told him, “Saul my father seeketh to kill thee: now therefore, I pray thee, take heed to thyself until the morning, and abide in a secret place, and hide thyself.”

Jonathan would have been next in line for the throne. You would think his loyalty lay with his daddy, but he saw the spirit was not on his father, it was on his brother David. His loyalty exceeded his own desires. That is the kind of friend to look for, and the lesson to learn from Jonathan.

precepts.point: Receive the law from his mouth and lay up his words in your heart. If you return to the Almighty you shall be built up and put away iniquity far from your tabernacle. This was our job, to build up our people.

note.label: Job 22: Acquaint Now Thyself With Him

precepts.why:
Eliphaz tells Job, “Acquaint now thyself with him, and be at peace: thereby good shall come unto thee.” You do not acquaint yourself with God by whispering that you love him. You hear from God through his prophets and his people to whom he gave his word, and Ecclesiasticus shows how that is done: “My son, if thou wilt, thou shalt be taught: and if thou wilt apply thy mind, thou shalt be prudent. If thou love to hear, thou shalt receive understanding: and if thou bow thine ear, thou shalt be wise”.

It means putting yourself where the word is taught. “Stand in the multitude of the elders; and cleave unto him that is wise. Be willing to hear every godly discourse; and let not the parables of understanding escape thee.” When you see a man of understanding, “get thee betimes unto him, and let thy foot wear the steps of his door.”

That is how you “Receive, I pray thee, the law from his mouth, and lay up his words in thine heart.” “Let thy mind be upon the ordinances of the Lord and meditate continually in his commandments: he shall establish thine heart, and give thee wisdom at thine owns desire.” Being acquainted with the Most High is hearing his law from his people and laying it up in the heart; that is where the peace and the good begin.
